First, we express $f(x)$ as a composite function

$$
f=2 \sin{\left(u \right)}, \qquad u=3 x - 1.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}f}{\mathrm{d}u}=2 \cos{\left(u \right)},\qquad \frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=3.
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d}f}{\mathrm{d}x}&=\frac{\mathrm{d}f}{\mathrm{d}u}\cdot\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}\\&=(2 \cos{\left(u \right)})\cdot(3)\\&=6 \cos{\left(u \right)}\\&=6 \cos{\left(3 x - 1 \right)}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

Therefore, the slope $m$ of $y=f(x)$ at $x=\frac{\pi }{6}$ is 

$$
m={f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{6})=0.
